gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, customer, quote or result that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research; baselines come from the business's data or are labelled as assumptions.
Pre-registration: every test has its metric, minimum volume, run time and scale/kill/iterate thresholds stated before launch; readouts apply the registered rule unchanged.
No false statistics: no p-values or 'statistically significant' claims from peeked, under-powered or unregistered tests; before/after results are labelled directional.
Honest and compliant: no deceptive fake doors, fake scarcity or payment without a clear refund promise; email tests only to contacts with consent or a lawful basis, with unsubscribe intact.

anchors.1: No decision named; hypothesis is a hunch ('let's see if blue works').
anchors.3: Hypothesis stated but not tied to evidence or to a decision.
anchors.5: Names the decision the test informs; hypothesis grounded in VoC counts, competitor gaps or audit findings.

anchors.1: Page-level A/B test on purchases at a traffic level that can't finish.
anchors.3: Reasonable test type but metric lower in the funnel than the volume supports.
anchors.5: Test type (message lab, smoke test, reply test, sequential, holdout, conversations) matched to volume; metric at the highest funnel step that still reflects the decision, with a secondary read.

anchors.3: A volume target with no maths or baseline.
anchors.5: Volume per variant computed from a sourced baseline and the target swing, maths shown, converted into a run time within about 6 weeks or the design changed.

anchors.3: Moderate changes that may not be detectable at this volume.
anchors.5: Big swings (offer, positioning, price, guarantee, channel) that could plausibly move the metric 30%+.

anchors.3: A single success threshold, no kill rule or guardrails.
anchors.5: Scale, kill and iterate-once thresholds stated as business thresholds; guardrail metrics with limits (refunds, unsubscribes, complaints, bounce, lead quality, margin).

anchors.1: Several changes at once; no mention of confounds.
anchors.3: One change, but audience, budget or timing not held constant.
anchors.5: One change per test; audience, budget, schedule and weekday mix matched; seasonality and other changes listed; no overlapping tests on one audience; algorithmic selection called out.

anchors.1: Claims a winner with no denominators, or moves the goalposts.
anchors.3: Numbers reported, rule applied loosely, no confidence label.
anchors.5: Denominators per variant, registered rule quoted and applied, strong/directional label with reasons, confounds, verbatim qualitative evidence, one next action.

anchors.1: Tests exceed the budget or hours, or run all at once.
anchors.5: Cost and hours stated per test within the owner's budget; backlog ranked by impact on the goal, confidence and cost, run sequentially on shared audiences.
